findings.text: The opening paragraphs tell a newcomer what Athena is, what a study is, and why this page exists: to show that Athena can explain an unfamiliar project with sources. A first-time reader can say what the site is within three paragraphs.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository.

findings.text: Someone who comes to the Athena site to learn about Athena gets one sentence about it. Almost everything else on the page is about a different project, firstmate. Only the lede shows that the page is a demonstration. Nothing explains what Athena produces apart from studies, or why someone would choose it.
This link sits in the header and speaks to an owner. A newcomer is not the owner and cannot tell who is meant or whether the link concerns them.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: The next steps are concrete and are linked from the top of the page. They do not list prerequisites, such as a Rust toolchain or AI model access, or say what the command will do to the reader's repository. A newcomer may hesitate to run it.
findings.source: Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh" and "athena ask "add a changelog""

findings.text: Key terms (captain, yolo, green, red, worker, agent) are defined before they are used, and the walkthrough "One piece of work, start to finish" is easy to follow. This makes a dense subject readable.
findings.source: Start here — "Words used first" and "What firstmate is"

findings.text: Some terms are used but never defined. The Glossary has no entry for "wake" or "endpoint", and the "stale wake" entry is circular. A newcomer cannot follow the relaunch card fully.
findings.source: t8 card: "A stale wake shows the worker is stuck... a secondmate re-reads its pin and needs none, and a secondmate with no endpoint is recovered by the spawn script"

findings.text: The Limits section uses Athena's internal wording ("recorded boundary", "edge"), and f3 says "A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths". This candour is useful, but it is written for Athena's operators rather than a first-time visitor.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f1: "The job gave no recorded boundary for running firstmate, so no failure or retry edge was observed"

findings.text: The page ends on internal build details about a folder the reader cannot see. This adds nothing for a newcomer.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"
